title: Watching a video
nerd: The app fetches the video in small segments over HTTPS (HTTP inside TLS inside TCP), and the server streams them back.

phone.kid: Your phone wants a cat video, so it writes a little request and sends it off.
phone.nerd: The app opens a TLS connection and sends an HTTP GET for the next video segment. The OS splits the data into TCP segments inside IP packets.

1995.title: Opening a web page with a picture
1995.kid: You open a web page with a picture on it.
1995.nerd: The browser fetches the page, then its picture, each with an HTTP/1.0 GET on a TCP connection of its own: plain HTTP, no TLS. SSL had just come out in Netscape, for shops. Video was stamp-sized clips (160 × 120, a few frames a second) that you downloaded before watching.

peek.page: Caught: a piece of the page

2010.title: Watching a small video
2010.kid: You ask for a small video.
2010.nerd: The player fetches the video as one file over plain HTTP (no TLS): a small 360p MP4 that starts playing while the rest is still on its way (progressive download). Video sites moved to HTTPS a few years later. The cache it came from was usually in a bigger city further away than today’s.
